feature.name: central_WA_motif
feature.description: For the 11-nt raw_sequence, inspect the central site and its immediate upstream base. Let the central site be position 5, and the upstream neighbor be position 4. Set the feature to 1 if position 4 is A or T and position 5 is A (i.e., the site is in a WA motif centered on the mutated base). Otherwise set it to 0.
feature.rationale: A strong, interpretable candidate at the root is whether the central mutated base lies in the Pol eta hotspot WA (W=A/T, followed by A at the target). In these 11-mer contexts, the site is the center base (position 5 in 0-based indexing of the 11-mer). Pol eta preferentially generates mutations at A/T bases in WA motifs, a hallmark more associated with germinal-center SHM activity. This feature focuses on one clear mechanism: local recruitment/signature of Pol eta at the mutation site. It is simple, biologically meaningful, and non-redundant at the root because no prior sequence-based split has been applied.

feature.name: pos_7_is_A
feature.description: Check if position 7 in raw sequence is A
feature.rationale: Basic sequence composition feature checking for A at position 7
feature.code:
def pos_7_is_A(X):
    return X['raw_sequence'].apply(lambda x: x[7] == 'A')

feature.name: upstream_overlapping_AID_WRC_motif
feature.description: For the 11-nt raw_sequence, inspect positions 3, 4, and 5, where position 5 is the central site. Set the feature to 1 if positions 3-5 form an AID WRC motif with the mutable C at position 4 immediately upstream of the central A. Operationally: position 3 must be A or T (W), position 4 must be A or G (R-equivalent here due to the node constraint on WA), and position 5 must be A. Otherwise set the feature to 0.
feature.rationale: This node already restricts sequences to those with a central WA motif, a classic Pol eta target. A non-redundant next split is to ask whether the mutated A is also embedded in an AID hotspot, because overlap between Pol eta WA and AID WRC contexts can distinguish mutational routes within these sequences. The most direct and interpretable version is the canonical WRC motif centered on the mutable C immediately upstream of the A, which in an 11-mer translates to checking positions 3-5 for WAA or TAC patterns consistent with positions 3=A/T, 4=A/G, and 5=A. Since all sequences at this node already have position 4=A/T and position 5=A, this feature specifically adds information about whether position 4 is a purine-compatible hotspot base and whether the upstream flanking base supports an AID hotspot. This captures a single biological mechanism: presence of an overlapping AID hotspot near the central WA site.
